applicability: Any positive integer n. Write n = a^2 + d where a = round(sqrt(n)) is the NEAREST whole square root, so |d| <= a. Then sqrt(n) ~= a + d/(2a). This estimate is never below sqrt(n) (it is the arithmetic mean of a and n/a, so am-gm gives (a + n/a)/2 >= sqrt(a * n/a) = sqrt(n), equality only when a^2 = n), and it overshoots by less than 1/(8a) - under 0.003 when a = 47. Two decimal places are therefore reliable for any a >= 40.
carry_case: Anchoring on a square that is not the nearest one. For n = 2232 with a = 40 instead of 47: 40 + (2232-1600)/80 = 40 + 7.9 = 47.90, which is 0.66 too high, versus 47.24 from a = 47 (true 47.2440). The estimate stays an upper bound, but the two-decimal accuracy is gone as soon as |d| > a.

universality_claim.claim: a + d/(2a) is never less than sqrt(n) for any a > 0, n > 0.
universality_claim.hypothesis_map: a + d/(2a) = (a + n/a)/2 with a > 0 and n/a > 0, both non-negative reals, so AM >= GM = sqrt(n).
universality_claim.finite_check: Error bound error < 1/(8a) checked exhaustively for n = 2..1000000 with a = round(sqrt(n)); |d| <= a checked on the same domain.
